sourcedFrom: PALMETTO DAGGER® OWNER'S MANUAL — P45-0001-00 — part number printed in the book's own back matter (2025)
cleanIntro: The Dagger is a striker-fired, Glock-pattern 9 mm pistol, and its strip has one step that catches people who have only ever stripped a Glock: PSA's own sequence pulls the slide back only 3–4 mm before the slide lock comes down. Go further and the trigger resets, and a reset trigger means starting the whole procedure again. The trigger must be pulled first, with the gun proven empty, because the striker has to be down before the slide will come off.

steps.title: ⛔ Clear it, and clear it the book's way — twice over
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger. Drop the magazine, lock the slide back, and check the chamber by eye and with a finger. PSA sends you to its own unloading section before the strip begins and again before any cleaning, because the very next step on this pistol is to pull the trigger.
steps.prose: Every page of this manual carries the same line across the top. The maker is telling you where he expects the mistakes to happen.
steps.quote: With the firearm empty and pointed in a safe direction, fully pull the trigger
steps.cite: PALMETTO DAGGER® OWNER'S MANUAL — P45-0001-00 — part number printed in the book's own back matter — Disassembly, printed p.17

steps.title: ⛔ Trigger pulled on the EMPTY gun — the striker must be down
steps.action: With the firearm empty and pointed somewhere safe, pull the trigger fully rearward. This drops the striker. On a Glock-pattern pistol the slide will not release while the striker is cocked, so this is not an optional flourish — it is what makes the next step possible.
steps.prose: If you find yourself pulling a trigger without having just checked the chamber, stop and check it again. The order exists for exactly this moment.
steps.caution: To remove the slide, complete the following procedure in this order.
steps.quote: With the firearm empty and pointed in a safe direction, fully pull the trigger
steps.cite: PALMETTO DAGGER® OWNER'S MANUAL — P45-0001-00 — part number printed in the book's own back matter — Disassembly, printed p.17

steps.title: ⛔ Slide back 3–4 mm ONLY — further resets the trigger
steps.action: Wrap your hand around the pistol and squeeze thumb and fingers together while pressing rearward on the rear sight with your index finger. You will feel the slide unlock. Let it travel back only about 3–4 mm — just enough that the slide overhangs the rear of the frame — and hold it there. More than that resets the trigger and you begin again from the clearing step.
steps.prose: This is the step that separates the Dagger from the pistol it copies. Small movement, held.
steps.quote: You will feel the slide unlock and begin to move rearward. Allow it to travel rearward until approximately 3 -4mm of the slide hang over the rear of the frame.
steps.cite: PALMETTO DAGGER® OWNER'S MANUAL — P45-0001-00 — part number printed in the book's own back matter — Disassembly, printed p.17

steps.title: Slide lock fully DOWN on BOTH sides, then slide forward off the frame
steps.action: With the slide held in that position, use your other hand to pull the slide lock fully downward on both sides at once. Then release the slide and let it run straight forward off the front of the frame.
steps.prose: Both sides, fully down. One side half-down is why a slide binds and why people start levering.
steps.quote: Using your support hand, pull the slide lock fully downward on both sides
steps.cite: PALMETTO DAGGER® OWNER'S MANUAL — P45-0001-00 — part number printed in the book's own back matter — Disassembly, printed p.17

steps.title: Recoil spring: press toward the MUZZLE, then rotate up
steps.action: Press the rear of the recoil spring assembly toward the muzzle about 3–4 mm, then rotate it upward to clear the lugs on the underside of the barrel. Release the pressure and lift the assembly out of the slide. It is captive but still under load — keep a thumb on it.
steps.prose: Toward the muzzle first. Rotating before compressing just jams the lugs.
steps.quote: Remove the assembly by pressing the rear of the assembly toward the muzzle roughly 3-4mm, then rotating it upward to clear the lugs on the bottom of the barrel
steps.cite: PALMETTO DAGGER® OWNER'S MANUAL — P45-0001-00 — part number printed in the book's own back matter — Disassembly, printed p.18

steps.title: Barrel out: lift by the locking lugs, forward then rearward and up
steps.action: Hold the slide inverted. Grip the barrel by the locking lugs on its underside, lift and push forward until roughly 6–8 mm of barrel stands out of the muzzle. Then keep lifting the rear while drawing the barrel back and up along the bore axis until it clears the slide.
steps.prose: Forward to unlock, back and up to leave. Trying to lift it straight out traps the lugs on the slide.
steps.aside: The pistol is now in the “field stripped” condition
steps.quote: Begin by holding the slide in an inverted orientation.
steps.cite: PALMETTO DAGGER® OWNER'S MANUAL — P45-0001-00 — part number printed in the book's own back matter — Disassembly, printed p.18

steps.title: Field strip complete — frame, slide, recoil assembly, barrel
steps.action: PSA calls this the field-stripped condition and stops here for routine cleaning. Going further into the slide is a separate, deeper procedure the book reserves for every 1,000 rounds.
steps.prose: Four parts on the mat. Anything more than four means you have gone past what the maker asks for after an ordinary range trip.
steps.quote: The pistol is now in the “field stripped” condition
steps.cite: PALMETTO DAGGER® OWNER'S MANUAL — P45-0001-00 — part number printed in the book's own back matter — Disassembly, printed p.18

deepSteps.title: The intervals PSA actually names
deepSteps.action: Clean after each use or 500 rounds, whichever comes first; once a year if the pistol is stored; and any time it meets water, sand or mud. Separately, every 1,000 rounds PSA wants the slide completely stripped for a deep clean — that is a different job from the field strip above.
deepSteps.prose: 500 to clean, 1,000 to strip the slide. Two numbers, two jobs.
deepSteps.aside: For every 1,000 rounds, the slide should be completely stripped down for a deep cleaning
deepSteps.quote: After each use or 500 rounds, whichever comes first
deepSteps.cite: PALMETTO DAGGER® OWNER'S MANUAL — P45-0001-00 — part number printed in the book's own back matter — Maintenance, printed p.23

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Keep cleaner OUT of the striker channel — it can cause a failure to fire
deepSteps.action: Hold the slide muzzle-down while you work, and keep removed fouling and excess cleaner-lubricant away from the striker area. PSA states plainly what happens if you do not: residue builds up during firing, and it can impair the trigger pull or cause failures to fire.
deepSteps.prose: This is the one place on a striker pistol where more oil is actively worse than less.
deepSteps.quote: Excess cleaner-lubricant around the striker can result in excessive residue build up during firing which can impair the trigger pull and/or cause failures to fire.
deepSteps.cite: PALMETTO DAGGER® OWNER'S MANUAL — P45-0001-00 — part number printed in the book's own back matter — Maintenance, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: Bore from the chamber end, and finish with a clean patch
deepSteps.action: Always start the rod from the chamber end. Alternate patch and brush until a patch comes out clean — if it does not, brush again. A single pass and a grey patch means the bore is still fouled.
deepSteps.prose: The test is the patch, not the number of passes.
deepSteps.aside: Follow up with another patch and bore cleaning to ensure all residue is cleaned from the bore - if the patch is not clean, repeat cleaning with the brush until a clean patch exits the barrel.
deepSteps.quote: Using a cleaning rod, pass a patch soaked in bore cleaner through the barrel
deepSteps.cite: PALMETTO DAGGER® OWNER'S MANUAL — P45-0001-00 — part number printed in the book's own back matter — Maintenance, printed p.24

deepSteps.title: ⛔ No oil on loose parts before they go back together
deepSteps.action: PSA is explicit that individual components are not oiled before reassembly. Lubrication happens at the points the book names, after the pistol is assembled. Oiling parts on the mat puts lubricant exactly where the previous step told you to keep it out of.
deepSteps.prose: The two instructions are the same instruction, seen from both ends.
deepSteps.quote: Do not oil individual components before reassembly.
deepSteps.cite: PALMETTO DAGGER® OWNER'S MANUAL — P45-0001-00 — part number printed in the book's own back matter — Maintenance, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: Barrel first, muzzle through the front of the slide
deepSteps.action: Slide inverted, barrel lugs facing up, muzzle through the hole at the front of the slide until 6–8 mm stands proud, then lower the chamber end and draw it rearward until it seats.
deepSteps.prose: It is the strip run backwards, and it should feel like it.
deepSteps.quote: insert the muzzle end of the barrel through the hole at the front of the slide
deepSteps.cite: PALMETTO DAGGER® OWNER'S MANUAL — P45-0001-00 — part number printed in the book's own back matter — Assembly, printed p.19

cleaning.name: BARREL AND BORE
tasks: Pass a bore-cleaner-soaked patch through from the CHAMBER end several times.
Follow with a brush and more bore cleaner to lift copper fouling and powder residue, then patch again until a patch comes out clean.
Finish with a lightly oiled patch to preserve the bore and rifling, then clean the outside of the barrel with a nylon brush and wipe it dry.

cleaning.name: SLIDE — BREECH FACE, EXTRACTOR CLAW, RAILS
tasks: Hold the slide MUZZLE DOWN so fouling and cleaner fall out rather than back into the striker channel.
Brush the breech face, the extractor claw and the slide rails with a nylon brush and cleaner-lubricant, then wipe and inspect.
⛔ Keep cleaner and fouling OUT of the striker area — see the deep steps.

cleaning.name: FRAME
tasks: Wipe the frame rails and the magazine well; check the slide lock moves freely on both sides and returns under its own spring.

reassembly: Slide inverted, barrel locking lugs UP: insert the muzzle through the hole at the front of the slide, push forward until 6–8 mm protrudes, then lower the chamber end in and slide it rearward until fully seated.
Recoil assembly forward end into the small hole at the front of the slide.
Press the rear of the assembly forward 3–4 mm to clear the barrel lugs, rotate it down into the rounded pocket on the front of the barrel lug, then release.
⛔ Do NOT oil individual components before reassembly — PSA lubricates at named points after the gun is together.
Slide onto the frame rails and run it back; the slide lock returns on its own.
Function-check before the pistol goes away.
fncheck: With the pistol reassembled and CLEAR, work the slide several times and watch that it returns fully to battery under spring pressure alone. Check the slide lock rises and falls freely on both sides. With the gun empty and pointed safely, pull the trigger for an audible break, then hold it back, cycle the slide, release and listen for the reset. Insert an empty magazine and confirm the slide locks back.
